thesis.core: Hengli shipbuilding continues to support a genuine earnings and order-book step change, but the equity still prices a sustained high-cycle outcome while expansion remains capital intensive.
thesis.variant_wedge: The operating inflection is real; the rejection remains valuation and financed-growth risk rather than weak fundamentals. The new RMB5.0bn debt-financing registration adds funding flexibility but does not itself improve intrinsic value and reinforces the need to distinguish operating cash flow from free cash flow.
thesis.normalized_earnings_basis: Retain the prior 2026E normalized EPS framework of RMB5.50/RMB7.50/RMB9.00 for bear/base/bull because no post-2026H1 disclosure changes normalized earnings sufficiently to justify a new model.

financed_growth_gate.interpretation: Customer advances support CFO, but H1 capex exceeded CFO and the newly accepted debt-financing registration increases financing optionality rather than proving higher free cash return.

normalized_earnings_basis.rationale: Fresh review retains the 2026-09-10 normalized earnings range; no new primary evidence warrants an upgrade.

catalysts: High-value ship orders convert into deliveries at or above H1 margins.
New yard and engine capacity reaches high utilization without material cost overruns.
Financing flexibility improves without debt, finance expense and capex outrunning sustainable free cash generation.
kill_thesis: Newbuild pricing or orders roll over before expanded capacity matures.
Delivery delays, cancellations, steel/FX pressure or mix deterioration compress normalized margin.
Debt, finance expense and capex continue to grow faster than sustainable free cash generation.
